title: Market-relative skill — what closing number would erase each signal
no_market_data_statement: No spread, total or price is imported from any source. Every 'market' figure in this file is either (a) blank because no official source publishes it, or (b) a breakeven threshold derived from the model's own error distribution and the assumed price. There is no market comparison anywhere in this repository, and this file does not create one.

model.method: shrunk points-for/against per game (k=3 prior games at the league mean), plus the league home edge measured from non-international games

week11_fair_lines.what_the_distance_means: A -110 bet only breaks even once our fair number is at least 0.63 points better (for a side) or 0.79 points better (for a total) than the number actually available. This distance is the same for every game: it is a property of the price and the league's scoring spread, not of this matchup. It is not a profit target and it is not evidence of an edge.

book_arithmetic.consequence: A forecast must clear 52.381% just to break even at an assumed -110. The repository's best measured spread hit rate (S1, 59.62% on 104 bets) has a 95% interval whose lower bound is 50.01%. See market_verdict.

market_verdict.verdict: NO ARM IS PROMOTED. 2 of the 18 arms that placed any bet have a hit-rate interval whose lower bound clears the 52.38% break-even rate: B11 (63.11%, low bound 53.47%), S8 (62.14%, low bound 52.49%). Neither is promotable. B11 is a naive rule that is not a registered strategy whose interval clears by only 1.09 percentage points, out of 18 arms tested (B01 is excluded because it placed none); at that margin a family correction removes it. S8 is a registered strategy whose interval clears by only 0.11 percentage points, out of 18 arms tested (B01 is excluded because it placed none); at that margin a family correction removes it. The point is not that these are bad numbers. It is that a 0.1-to-1.0 point margin over break-even, on about 100 bets, selected from nineteen arms, is indistinguishable from luck, and the repository would be manufacturing a signal by promoting it. What promotion requires is a price and an out-of-sample season, not a slightly higher hit rate.

caveats: The Week 11 numbers are originated before those games are played. They are predictions, not results, and they carry no market comparison.
Sigma is a single league-wide constant. Prior sessions flagged the same choice (LF-03); it is inherited, not re-litigated here.

The break-even cushion assumes our error is unbiased and independent of the market's. If the model is systematically biased, the cushion is optimistic. There is no way to test that without a price series.
Nothing in this file authorises a stake. It prices the hurdle, and states that the hurdle has not been cleared on evidence.
